I've been wanting to build a small server for a while, now I've finally decided I want a simple with R studio or something similar. What's a good linux for a server?
Learning is great, making your life needlessly difficult not so much. Just use the OS that there is ample documentation for and be done with it.

If you want lean and powerful, I'd suggest Slackware.
If you want more features, but still high stability, I'd suggest Debian.
Use whatever you feel most comfortable with. Really, there is no "best" option.

Since you already use a Debian based system, I strongly recommend sticking with a system that uses .deb files :)

It looks like R Studio has .deb files downloadable directly from their website. This is a good sign. It also appears that it has a GUI which confuses me. In my opinion, servers rarely have X installed on them. If you want X on your server then I'm again going to suggest Ubuntu or Debian, probably Ubuntu or XUbuntu since you're more familiar with it.

TL;DR

Ubuntu

Go with Debian. And in a year, a BSD ;)

Only if you are running something quite large and you've been at this for a while. It's better for porting from more common systems after a project has matured. I have to mention it for the few people who may not understand/know. These are modem speed tests. Not a direct connection to your PC. You might have X download/upload, but that doesn't mean you're getting X to your computer. Make sure, if you notice sluggish speeds, that you check your ethernet cables.

My situation was this: I was cheap. I decided to run an ethernet cord outside up to the second floor, then back in. This wasn't a weather-proof line. After a couple of years of weathering the line began to deteriorate. I noticed my speeds were dropping and I would constantly speedtest to see if it would say anything different. It never did. I figured out it was the cable when I took my laptop down and ran some internet heavy tests. Download/uploading files.
